text:
ashley: Heads-up — Acme reported repeated 599s when calling /v1/generate with very large single-request prompts. They saw a burst this morning (~10:12 UTC) where ~30% of requests returned 599 or connection closed. Customer provided repro + payload.
ashley: Repro (from customer):
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate 
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' 
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' 
  -d '{"model":"redwood-2-large","prompt":"<120k chars here>","max_tokens":512,"stream":false}'
```
Response: connection closed (599) after ~12s. Request id: r-0a1b2c3d4e. Edge: usw2.

jason: Can you paste the exact raw edge log lines we have for r-0a1b2c3d4e? want upstream error and backend status.

ashley: log snippet:
```
[2026-03-17T10:12:14Z] r-0a1b2c3d4e edge-proxy accept body 118kB
[2026-03-17T10:12:26Z] r-0a1b2c3d4e upstream runtime connection reset by peer (EPIPE)
[2026-03-17T10:12:26Z] r-0a1b2c3d4e response 599 connection closed
```

tony: Useful. My initial hypothesis: very large prompt + non-streaming triggers large KV cache allocation and memory pressure in the runtime. When the runtime hits a memory guard, it tears down the connection instead of returning a structured 5xx. Also seeing similar behavior in canary earlier for oversized payloads.

tony: Quick repro steps I suggest we try locally: 1) run model on local dev runtime with same model & config 2) send same huge prompt (non-streaming) 3) monitor /proc/mem and runtime logs for OOM guard 4) toggle prefix_cache: false and re-run. Example command:
```
# run from infra box
ab -n 1 -c 1 -p huge_payload.json https://localhost:8080/v1/generate
```
If disabling prefix cache avoids the reset, confirms kvcache allocation path.

eli: Customer also reported SDK v0.20 default retries=5 with no jitter. That can amplify the problem (many large requests retried concurrently). Recommend telling customer to set maxRetries=1-2 and enable exponential jitter as a temporary mitigation. Also suggest they try stream=true — streaming keeps the connection active and forces incremental token production which avoids buffering huge X bytes server-side.

eli: Suggested temporary guidance to send to Acme (I already pinged them):
- set SDK option maxRetries=2 and backoff with jitter
- if possible, split prompt into two calls (pre-context + generate) or enable streaming=true
- set request timeout to 45s on client, and log request_id on failures

jason: We'll also validate edge body size limits. Current ingress limit is 16MB; if the customer is hitting it we should return 413 instead of teardown. But logs show 118kB, so not body-size threshold here. More likely runtime eviction path.

deploy-bot: Canary rollout 2026-03-17T10:03:00: runtime patch rtx-evict-2026-03-17 applied to 5% canary (kvcache eviction tweak + defensive close-to-error -> structured 5xx).

ashley: I relayed the mitigation to the customer (split + reduce retries). They applied and reported immediate reduction in failures (so far ~20 calls). Asking for an ETA on full fix.

jason: Patch is on canary; monitoring metrics now. If canary p99 error rate stays < baseline for 30m we'll promote. Tentative ETA for full rollout: 4-6 hours after canary stability. I'll update here when promoted.

marina: Heads-up for docs: we should add a short note in "Best practices for large prompts" covering: prefer streaming, reduce client retries, and split prompts. I'll open a docs PR after final confirmation.

tony: Follow-ups for eng: 1) add better telemetry when runtime evicts due to kvcache growth (emit structured 5xx with code KVCACHE_EVICT) 2) ensure edge maps these to 502/503 not raw 599.

ashley: OK keeping thread open. If anyone sees regression or customer mentions new request_ids, drop here. Acme contact is on standby for verification. :thumbsup:
